text: Since the disputed 2020 election, Belarus's authorities have carried out widespread, systematic repression of critics: UN Human Rights Council-mandated experts documented arbitrary arrests, torture and persecution, some of it amounting to crimes against humanity. More than 1,100 people remained political prisoners in late 2025, facing ill-treatment, isolation and torture.
short: UN-mandated experts: Belarus's repression of critics includes arbitrary detention and torture, partly amounting to crimes against humanity; 1,100+ political prisoners in late 2025.

source.name: UN News: Belarus: Violations remain ‘widespread and systematic’, says independent expert group
source.quote: authorities have been committing widespread human rights violations, some amounting to crimes against humanity, as part of a systematic campaign to silence political opposition.

additionalSources.name: Human Rights Watch: World Report 2026 - Belarus (events of 2025)
additionalSources.note: The chapter also reports that in December 2025 at least 1,110 people remained behind bars on politically motivated grounds.
additionalSources.quote: Political prisoners continue to face ill-treatment, isolation, and torture.
